reviewPolicy: Only genuine screenshots from reviewed official documentation, attached by explicit question match. Preserve provenance and original bytes; no invented Salesforce UI or generic fallback. Inherit full-explanation entitlement and 180-day review expiry.

resources.title: Edit a record type’s picklist choices
resources.description: Compare available values with the choices selected for one record type.
resources.reviewNote: Genuine screenshot from the linked public Trailhead lesson, visually inspected on 2026-10-16. Example data and original annotations belong to Salesforce. Labels and available options can differ by release and org.

screenshot.alt: Salesforce Picklist Values editor with Available Values on the left, Selected Values on the right, and a highlighted Remove arrow.
screenshot.caption: The lesson highlights removing values from this record type’s selected list. This changes the allowed subset, not the field’s shared value definition.
screenshot.navigationPath: Setup → Object Manager → Object → Record Types → Record type → Picklist field
keyPoints: Selected Values are the choices offered for that record type.
Available Values and the Add/Remove controls let an administrator adjust the subset.

resources.title: Compare available and selected values
resources.description: See the record-type-specific subset beside other available field values.
resources.reviewNote: Genuine screenshot from the linked public Trailhead lesson, visually inspected on 2026-10-16. Example data and original annotations belong to Salesforce. Labels and available options can differ by release and org.

screenshot.alt: Salesforce Picklist Values editor with three available choices and four selected partner-related choices, highlighted in the original lesson.
screenshot.caption: This partner example shows that a field can retain other available choices while one record type offers only selected values.
screenshot.navigationPath: Setup → Object Manager → Object → Record Types → Record type → Picklist field
keyPoints: The right-hand list is the allowed subset for this record type.
A global value set defines reusable values; this screen selects which values a record type offers.

resources.title: Read and Edit permissions for individual fields
resources.description: Compare readable, editable, and hidden fields in a permission set.
resources.reviewNote: Genuine screenshot from the linked public Trailhead lesson, visually inspected on 2026-10-16. Example data and original annotations belong to Salesforce. Labels and available options can differ by release and org.

screenshot.alt: Salesforce Field Permissions table showing Field Name, API Name, Read Access, and Edit Access; some rows are read-only and others have neither permission.
screenshot.caption: The Candidate example separates field visibility from editability. It does not replace the page-layout check when troubleshooting a missing field.
screenshot.navigationPath: Setup → Permission Sets → Permission set → Object Settings → Object → Edit
keyPoints: Read Access and Edit Access are independent controls to inspect.
Compare a row with Read only against a row with both boxes checked.

resources.title: See a validation error when saving a record
resources.description: See how a validation rule blocks an invalid save with a useful error message.
resources.reviewNote: Genuine screenshot from the linked public Trailhead lesson, visually inspected on 2026-10-16. Example data and original annotations belong to Salesforce. Labels and available options can differ by release and org.

screenshot.alt: Salesforce Account edit form showing an Account Number value of 1234 and an error explaining that the number must be eight characters long.
screenshot.caption: This is the lesson’s account-number example. Use the question’s own conditions and formula; the pictured rule is not the exact rule for every scenario.
screenshot.navigationPath: Record page → Edit → Enter values → Save
keyPoints: The error prevents the invalid record from being saved.
The visible message explains what must be corrected; it does not automatically change the entered value.

resources.title: Choose what a Get Records element retrieves
resources.description: See object selection and condition controls in the Get Records element.
resources.reviewNote: Genuine screenshot from the linked public Trailhead lesson, visually inspected on 2026-10-16. Example data and original annotations belong to Salesforce. Labels and available options can differ by release and org.

screenshot.alt: Salesforce New Get Records panel showing a label, API Name, Opportunity Contact Role object, and All Conditions Are Met condition requirement.
screenshot.caption: The example queries Opportunity Contact Role records. Your scenario may use another object, but the Get Records controls perform the same retrieval role.
screenshot.navigationPath: Setup → Flows → Flow Builder → Add Element → Get Records
keyPoints: Object selects the type of records to query.
Conditions identify matching records; this differs from creating or updating records.

resources.title: Choose how many records and fields to store
resources.description: Compare first-record and all-record results, plus the field-storage options.
resources.reviewNote: Genuine screenshot from the linked public Trailhead lesson, visually inspected on 2026-10-16. Example data and original annotations belong to Salesforce. Labels and available options can differ by release and org.

screenshot.alt: Salesforce Get Records settings with descending CreatedDate sort, Only the first record selected, and Automatically store all fields selected.
screenshot.caption: This example retrieves the most recently created matching record and stores its fields for later flow elements.
screenshot.navigationPath: Flow Builder → Get Records → Sort and record-storage settings
keyPoints: First record versus All records changes whether the result is a single record or a collection.
The field-storage choices control the data available to later elements.
